summary: Found by the lead while running this session.

findings.title: The token ledger did not see helpers started by a workflow (fixed: CB-210)
findings.evidence: `brain ledger` printed '1 helper(s) ... $3.42' while seven workflow helpers were running; their transcripts are in <session>/subagents/workflows/<run>/agent-*.jsonl. After the fix the same moment read '7 helper(s) ... $13.14'.
findings.proposed_fix: Done: common.helper_transcripts finds agent-*.jsonl at any depth under subagents/ and ignores a workflow's journal.jsonl; the session-end hook uses it.

findings.title: The session-end hook rewrites a tracked inbox file after every turn, so the tree is dirty after every turn and each turn ends with a request to commit
findings.evidence: After the first turn of this session `git status` showed `?? learning/inbox/2026-11-10-<session>.jsonl`; the cloud session's own stop check then answered 'There are untracked files in the repository. Please commit and push'. The history already holds three 'learn: session records' commits from one build session.
findings.proposed_fix: The hook keeps capturing (a session can die without `close`), but into a path git ignores: learning/inbox/.live/<date>-<session>.jsonl (add learning/inbox/.live/ to .gitignore). `brain close` and `checkpoint --push` write the tracked record as today and delete the live file. The repair of an unclosed session at the next boot reads the live file first, then the transcript. learn.pending_session_records also reads the live file, so `close` keeps what an earlier capture knew.
findings.acceptance: Tests: the hook leaves `git status --porcelain` empty in a git brain; close after a hook capture writes one tracked record with the same totals and removes the live file; repair uses a live file when the transcript is gone.

findings.title: A copy of the brain made with cp -a keeps the real remote: an auditor's scratch copy pushed three test records to this branch
findings.evidence: Commit 89b5624 'learn: session records' on origin/claude/optimistic-newton-sh6lcx came from a scratch copy running `checkpoint --push`; reverted in 9e4b158. Two other auditors' copies also tried to push before they re-pointed their remotes.
findings.proposed_fix: Engine side is package A (push_brain_records: only this session's files, never from a copy under the temp folder, honour BRAIN_NO_PUSH). Instruction side: method/brain-work.md and hr/GUIDELINES.md say a scratch copy of the brain is made with `git clone --no-hardlinks <brain> <copy> && git -C <copy> remote remove origin` (or with BRAIN_NO_PUSH=1), never cp -a.
findings.acceptance: grep -q 'remote remove origin' method/brain-work.md; the package A tests for push_brain_records.

findings.title: Owner's instruction, 2026-11-10: the project repository carries everything a new chat needs to continue; make that folder explain itself
findings.evidence: The owner, in this session: "You will save plenty of files in the other repo, the project repo, that will tell you that information. Do not save that in the main brain repo, because then we will just have many unrelated files with saved information there." `brain init` installs .brain/ (STATE.md, PLAN.md, DECISIONS.md, requirements.jsonl, project.json, memory/lessons.jsonl, ext/, log/), CLAUDE.md stub, STATUS.md and NEEDS_YOU.md, but nothing in the project says which file holds what, that the last chat may have saved on another branch, or which branch and commit a checkpoint was written on.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) contract.py: init, adopt and migrate also write .brain/README.md, a map of at most 25 lines: what each file in .brain/ is for, who writes it, and how a new chat continues (run boot; if boot names a newer saved state on another branch, run `brain resume --adopt`; with no brain attached, read STATE.md, PLAN.md and HANDOVER.md). It is created only when missing, so existing projects keep theirs and the frozen fixtures still validate. (b) contract/template/CLAUDE.stub.md: one sentence in the managed block: the last chat may have saved its work on its own branch; boot says so and `brain resume --adopt` continues from it. Keep the stub under its 2,000-byte cap. (c) state.py: each checkpoint records the branch and short commit it was written on in STATE.md (two fields, read back by resume and boot, shown in the handover line), so the state says where it came from whichever branch it is read on. (d) Nothing about a project is written to the brain beyond what I-05 already allows (family and salted hashes in inbox records).
findings.acceptance: Tests: init writes .brain/README.md and a second init leaves an edited one alone; the three frozen fixtures still validate (tests/test_fixtures.py unchanged); the stub is under its cap and `brain budget` passes; a checkpoint on branch X records X and the commit, and resume prints them; the continuity rehearsal (core-20) passes.
